Accessibility

This is the report for the course website. See also the accessibility overview and the report for the course’s PrairieLearn content.

Accessibility Statement

We want every student in IS445 (Data Visualization) to be able to use the course materials. This page documents how the course website currently measures up against the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at Levels A and AA, including the places where it falls short. We are actively working through the known issues listed below.

If any part of this website is a barrier for you, please contact the instructor at jnaiman@illinois.edu. You do not need to wait for a fix to be published: we will provide the material in a format that works for you. Students who need accessibility-related academic adjustments should also see the Accessibility Statement in the syllabus and contact Disability Resources and Educational Services (DRES).

Conformance Report

This report follows the structure of the VPAT® 2.4Rev WCAG edition.

   
Name of product IS445 Data Visualization course website
Location http://localhost:4009/is445_bcu_fall2026 (source: https://github.com/UIUC-iSchool-DataViz/is445_bcu_fall2026)
Report date November 2026
Description A static website, built with Jekyll and hosted on GitHub Pages, that publishes the course syllabus, weekly overview pages, lecture slides, and Jupyter notebooks.
Contact Jill Naiman, jnaiman@illinois.edu
Standard WCAG 2.1 Level A and Level AA

Scope

The report covers the four kinds of page that make up this website:

  • Regular pages: the home page, the syllabus, and the weekly overview pages.
  • Lecture slides: slide decks written in Markdown and displayed in the browser with reveal.js 4.0.2.
  • Notebook viewer: Jupyter notebooks displayed in the browser with nbviewer.js.
  • Downloadable files: notebooks, Python files, data files, and one PDF.

The report does not cover the separate platforms the course links to (Canvas, PrairieLearn, Slack, GitHub, YouTube, and Vimeo) or other external websites. Each of those is responsible for its own accessibility; where one is available, please see that platform’s own accessibility documentation, for example PrairieLearn’s conformance report.

Evaluation methods

This evaluation was a manual review of the website’s source code: the page templates, the style sheets, the Markdown source of the 26 published slide decks, and the notebook viewer page. Counts of images, videos, and similar items quoted in the remarks come from that source. Colour contrast was calculated from the colour values in the style sheets.

The following have not yet been done, and ratings may change once they are:

  • testing with a screen reader (such as VoiceOver, NVDA, or JAWS);
  • hands-on keyboard-only testing in a browser;
  • a scan with an automated checker (such as axe or WAVE);
  • a review of caption quality on the embedded third-party videos;
  • a review of each individual image, chart, animated GIF, and notebook output.

Terms

The terms used in the “Conformance level” column are defined as follows:

  • Supports: the functionality of the website has at least one method that meets the criterion without known defects, or meets it with equivalent facilitation.
  • Partially Supports: some functionality of the website does not meet the criterion.
  • Does Not Support: the majority of the website’s functionality does not meet the criterion.
  • Not Applicable: the criterion is not relevant to the website.

Status

The “Status” column in each table tracks our progress on that criterion. Each entry lists the files to look at, linked to the course’s GitHub repository.

  • To do a known problem that nobody has started fixing. In the tables, write s="todo".
  • In progress a fix has been started but is not finished. Write s="progress".
  • Needs check no known problem, but the rating has not been confirmed by testing. Write s="check".
  • Done fixed or confirmed. Write s="done".
  • No action nothing to do. Write s="none".

1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) Partially Supports Body text on regular pages (about 8.9:1) and slide text (about 15.9:1) exceed the 4.5:1 minimum, and body links on regular pages just meet it (about 4.55:1). Exceptions: links in the page footer (about 4.35:1) and selected topic tags on the home page (white on green, about 2.2:1) fall below it. Text inside images and the notebook viewer’s colours have not been measured. To do
  • _includes/footer.html: footer link colour
  • assets/style.css: selected tag colours
  • nbv.html: measure viewer colours
1.4.4 Resize Text Partially Supports Text on regular pages can be enlarged to 200% with browser zoom. Lecture slides cannot: the slide template disables pinch-zoom on touch devices, and reveal.js rescales each slide to fit the window, which cancels out browser zoom. To do
  • _layouts/lecture.html: remove user-scalable=no; review Reveal scaling settings
1.4.5 Images of Text Partially Supports Most code in the slides is real text. Some slides show screenshots of code, terminal output, or file contents where text could be used instead. To do
  • Slide decks to check (table below): replace screenshots of code with text
1.4.10 Reflow Partially Supports Regular pages reflow to a single column on narrow screens, although the navigation menu is then unavailable (see 2.1.1) and wide syllabus tables need horizontal scrolling. Lecture slides have a fixed 1024 by 768 layout that shrinks to fit the screen instead of reflowing. The notebook viewer needs horizontal scrolling for wide code and output. To do
  • _layouts/lecture.html: fixed 1024 by 768 slide size
  • _includes/header.html: small-screen menu
  • syllabus.md: wide tables
  • nbv.html: wide code and output
1.4.11 Non-text Contrast Partially Supports Controls and focus indicators use browser and framework defaults that meet the 3:1 minimum. The contrast of lines, marks, and labels within individual charts and diagrams shown in the slides has not been reviewed. Needs check
  • Slide decks to check (table below): check contrast within charts and diagrams
1.4.12 Text Spacing Partially Supports Regular pages do not restrict text spacing. On lecture slides, which have a fixed size, increased spacing can push text off the slide. Not yet tested in a browser. Needs check
  • assets/styles.less: test slides with increased text spacing
  • _layouts/lecture.html: slide size settings
1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus Partially Supports Regular pages show no custom pop-up content. Tooltips on the interactive charts in two slide decks disappear when the pointer moves onto them and cannot be dismissed from the keyboard. To do
  • week08/lecture08p2.md: chart tooltips
2.4.5 Multiple Ways Supports The home page lists every week’s lectures and materials, each weekly page lists its own, and the navigation bar appears on all regular pages. There is no search. No action
2.4.6 Headings and Labels Supports Headings describe the content that follows them, and nearly every slide has a heading. No action
2.4.7 Focus Visible Supports The website does not remove the browser’s default focus indicator. Not yet confirmed by hands-on testing. Needs check
  • assets/style.css: confirm focus outline is visible on every control
3.1.2 Language of Parts Supports Content is written in English. No passages in other languages were identified. No action
3.2.3 Consistent Navigation Supports The navigation bar is the same, in the same order, on every regular page. No action
3.2.4 Consistent Identification Supports Lectures, notebooks, data, and libraries are labelled and marked with the same icons throughout. No action
3.3.3 Error Suggestion Not Applicable The website has no forms or other user input. No action
3.3.4 Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data) Not Applicable The website handles no legal, financial, or personal data. No action
4.1.3 Status Messages Partially Supports reveal.js announces the content of each new slide to screen readers. If a notebook fails to load, the notebook viewer shows a blank page and gives no message to any user. To do
  • nbv.html: show a message when a notebook fails to load

Downloadable files

Jupyter notebooks, Python files, and data files are provided for students to download and run in their own software; their accessibility there depends on that software. The repository holds one PDF (15 pages of Jekyll tour notes in the Week 9 folder). It is not tagged for screen readers, so its headings, reading order, and images are not exposed to assistive technology.
